short: Reported spacetime savings over kickmix and Häner

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Primitives.Arcsin:QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_k25_const_cost
lean.plain: Benchmark spacetime bound and primitive Toffoli count
lean.annotation: Appendix F.2 estimates $440{,}576$ $T$ gates for two dominant blocks on a workspace of 245 qubits. Dividing that product by the final upper bound gives $(440{,}576/3{,}698)\cdot(245/100)\approx292$. This is the basis of the paper’s reported factor of about 290.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_correctness
lean.plain: Uniform approximation and exact modular addition
lean.annotation: The benchmark proof gives uniform absolute error at most $1.25\times10^{-7}$ on the valid 25-bit grid and exact modular accumulation. The reported Häner comparison uses 35-bit arithmetic and an error estimate of about $10^{-6}$ based on sampled square-root errors. The two error levels and the partial baseline accounting belong to that numerical comparison.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Primitives.Arcsin:QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_k25_const_cost
lean.plain: Benchmark spacetime bound and primitive Toffoli count
lean.annotation: The published costs are $4{,}152$ and $3{,}698$ $T$ gates at the same width. The change is all in the combined lookup-and-add stage in Fig. S11(b). The early lookup falls by 644, the adder falls by 60, and the later lookup rises by 250. The net change of 454 gives the reported overall reduction of about $10.9\%$.

statements.markdown: leading to a further overall $11\%$ lower cost
